citations.claim: first energy violation: total energy swung to -292.13 while bodies are 0.105 apart, deep inside softening
two steps before, separation 0.70 and energy near initial (1.13), then one step before separation 0.43 and energy already -102, showing runaway during plunge
companion speed grows 13.15 to 18.47 over last two steps as pair falls together

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.013564776551038028 to 0.003 with all else identical; finer resolution of pericenter removes the energy drift

explanation: Two heavy bodies on a plunging orbit undergo a close encounter well inside the softening length (d=0.10 < eps=0.3 at step 32). Substeps grow only 12->13->16, insufficient to resolve the rapidly rising acceleration/velocity at pericenter with dt~0.0136. Leapfrog therefore gains large energy error: kinetic and |potential| both inflate to ~3500 while net energy swings from +26 to -292, violating energy_conserved. Reducing dt resolves the encounter and conserves energy, confirming under-resolved close approach as cause.
vision_note: Two separate blue bodies visible in step 29 move closer in steps 30-31 and overlap as a single blob by step 32. Their short trails show rapid motion during this close approach and apparent collision.
